land.text: the 1015 shape without its Jaén district: the kingdom 'formed in al-Andalus in 1013' on Granada, before Habbus 'attacked Cabra and Jaén' c. 1028-1029

predecessors.note: The page: 'formed in al-Andalus (in present-day Spain) in 1013' by Zawi ibn Ziri when the Zirids moved to Granada. Cliopatria's row starts in 1015.

land.text: Granada city and its district, 'captured by the Almoravids in September 1090'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Granada row to 1093.
Málaga had been Tamim's separate realm since 1073 and was conquered by the Almoravids in 1090 (Taifa of Málaga page); it is not part of Granada's end land.

capitals.name: Granada
capitals.note: 'The kingdom was centered on Granada, its capital.' The infobox dates the Zirid move to Granada to 1013.

rulers.name: Abdallah ibn Buluggin
rulers.note: Badis's grandson, 'between seven and nine years old' at accession; surrendered the city to the Almoravids and went into exile in Aghmat.

correction.text: the 1015 shape without its Jaén district: the kingdom 'formed in al-Andalus in 1013' on Granada, before Habbus 'attacked Cabra and Jaén' c. 1028-1029

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page founds the kingdom in 1013 ('formed in al-Andalus ... in 1013'), Cliopatria starts in 1015, and Cliopatria's first outline already reaches 38.5 N (Jaén province) although the page has Habbus 'attacked Cabra and Jaén around 1028-1029, expanding north'. The page gives no area; the outline here is Cliopatria's without Jaén, years 1013-1027.

20,906 km2: right for the kingdom after Habbus's northward push (1028-1029, Cabra and Jaén) until the annexation of Málaga (1056), so the years are 1028-1055 only; 1013-1027 is the narrower 1013 keyframe and 1056-1065 the wider one. No infobox area to compare. The same outline is used through 1065 although the Zirids 'took much of' Almería's land in 1038 and 'also defeated the Abbadids ... near Écija, gaining land to the west' in 1039: the page names no places for either, so nothing is added.

correction.text: Granada with Málaga and the coast to the west (24,629 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Zirid conquest of Málaga occurred in 1056' (Taifa of Granada page: 'Badis annexed Málaga in 1056'; the Taifa of Málaga page says 1057 and its infobox 'To Granada: 1057-1073'). Cliopatria adds Málaga only in 1066, ten years late; its 24,629 km2 outline (to 5.1 W and 36.5 N) is the Granada-plus-Málaga shape. No page gives an area.

24,629 km2: Granada with Málaga, which the pages put in Zirid hands from 1056/57 to 1073. Years 1066-1071 stand; the outline's western edge, which touches the 1065 Seville conquest of Ronda (Taifa of Ronda), is not described by any page opened.

correction.text: the 1072 shape without Málaga, which 'went to Tamim ben Buluggin' in 1073

keyframe_review.note: 23,660 km2 still contains Málaga, but 'Málaga went to Tamim ben Buluggin ben Badis' in 1073 ('Tamim period (1073-1090)'; the Granada page has Tamim declare independence without a year). From 1073 the kingdom is the 1072 outline without Málaga province. 1072 itself stands as drawn.

correction.text: unchanged outline, years 1085-1090 only; the Almoravids hold it from September 1090

keyframe_review.note: 9,549 km2: Granada city and district without Málaga and without the northern and eastern edges of the 1072 outline. The pages date neither the loss of those edges nor their new holder (page silent); this is the shape for 1085-1090 only, because the kingdom ended when 'Granada was captured by the Almoravids in September 1090', not in 1093. No infobox area.

region.text: the 1015 shape without its Jaén district: the kingdom 'formed in al-Andalus in 1013' on Granada, before Habbus 'attacked Cabra and Jaén' c. 1028-1029

ledger.note: 1013: Zawi ibn Ziri founds the Zirid kingdom of Granada. 'formed in al-Andalus (in present-day Spain) in 1013'; the capital is Granada. Cliopatria starts the row in 1015.

region.text: the Jaén district inside Cliopatria's 1015 shape: Habbus 'attacked Cabra and Jaén around 1028-1029, expanding north'

ledger.note: c. 1028-1029: Habbus pushes north into Jaén. He 'attacked Cabra and Jaén around 1028-1029, expanding north'; the page does not name who held the district (Cliopatria's Córdoba is the neighbour on the north), and 'attacked' is read as 'took'. Cliopatria's 1015 outline already contains the district.

region.text: Seville (Aznalcázar, Tocina, Triana) and the plain round Écija

ledger.note: 1036: Habbus attacks Seville. 'on or around 30 August 1036', with allies from Almería and Écija, he took Aznalcázar and Tocina and burned Triana.

region.text: the taifa of Almería as a whole

ledger.note: 1038: Granada makes Almería a vassal. After Zuhayr was defeated at al-Funt in 1038 the Zirids 'turned Almeria into a vassal state for several years' and took 'much of his land' (no places named). The Almería page has Zuhayr killed by a revolt of his own troops in 1038 and a Valencian occupation 'To Valencia: 1038-1042', which the Granada page does not mention.

region.text: Seville (Aznalcázar, Tocina, Triana) and the plain round Écija

ledger.note: 1039: Zirid victory near Écija. 'the Zirids also defeated the Abbadids of Seville in battle near Écija', gaining land 'to the west' (no places named). The Taifa of Málaga page calls Écija a Malagan victory supported by Almería, Granada and Carmona.

region.text: the taifa of Almería as a whole

ledger.note: c. 1041: Almería is its own master again. The Granada page gives only 'for several years'; the Almería page's rulers list has Ma'n ben Muhammad ben Sumadih from 1041 and a Valencian period ending 1042, so 1041 is a bridge (page silent).

1056: Badis annexes Málaga. 'Badis annexed Málaga in 1056, after Hammudid rule collapsed there' (Zirid conquest of Málaga: 'occurred in 1056', the Hammudid Yahya III al-Mahdi defeated; the Taifa of Málaga page says 1057). The pages disagree on who governed it: Granada's page 'his son Buluggin', the conquest page 'his brother Tamim'.

1073: Málaga passes to Tamim. 'Málaga went to Tamim ben Buluggin ben Badis' while Abd Allah gained Granada (Tamim period 1073-1090; infobox 'To Granada: 1057-1073'); the Granada page says Tamim, Abdallah's brother, 'declared independence' and gives no year.

minus.text: the 1072 shape without Málaga, which 'went to Tamim ben Buluggin' in 1073
Granada without Málaga and without its northern and eastern edges (9,549 km2)

region.text: the northern and eastern edges of the 1072 outline

ledger.note: 1085: Cliopatria narrows Granada to its core. The pages date no loss of the northern (Jaén) and eastern edges and name no taker (Cliopatria shows Seville, Algeciras and Almería as neighbours from 1085, the Granada page only the parias Alfonso VI made Granada and Seville pay in the 1080s and the defeat at Cabra in 1079); the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Granada without Málaga and without its northern and eastern edges (9,549 km2)

ledger.note: 1090: the Almoravids take Granada. 'captured by the Almoravids in September 1090'; Abdallah 'surrendered the city to them without a fight', was detained, lost his property and went into exile in Aghmat.

region.text: Granada without Málaga and without its northern and eastern edges (9,549 km2)

ledger.note: 1090: the independent kingdom of Granada ends; the land passes to the Almoravids (see the loss event). Cliopatria keeps a Granada shape to 1093.

wars.name: Zirid–Abbadid war of 1036-1039 (Battle of Écija)

zones.text: Seville (Aznalcázar, Tocina, Triana) and the plain round Écija

wars.outcome: Habbus took Aznalcázar and Tocina and burned Triana in 1036; the Zirids 'defeated the Abbadids of Seville in battle near Écija' in 1039, gaining land to the west.
wars.note: The Taifa of Málaga page counts Écija (1039) as a Malagan victory supported by Almería, Granada and Carmona; the war's name is the researcher's, the battle is a linked article on the Granada page that was not opened.

wars.name: Battle of al-Funt

zones.text: Zuhayr's land in the Almería taifa

wars.outcome: Zuhayr of Almería was defeated; the Zirids took much of his land and made Almería a vassal state for several years.
wars.note: Linked article, not opened; Almería's page says Zuhayr was killed in 1038 by a revolt of his own troops after he angered his Granadan allies.

wars.name: Zirid conquest of Málaga
wars.outcome: Badis defeated the Hammudid king of Málaga in battle and annexed his kingdom.
wars.note: 1056 on the conquest page and the Granada page, 1057 on the Taifa of Málaga page.

wars.name: Battle of Cabra
wars.outcome: 'The Zirids were defeated in the Battle of Cabra in 1079 against the forces of Seville.'
wars.note: No border change is stated; the page describes frequent wars with Seville after 1066 without dates.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Granada

zones.text: Granada without Málaga and without its northern and eastern edges (9,549 km2)

wars.outcome: The Almoravids took Granada in September 1090 without a fight; Abdallah went into exile.
wars.note: Abdallah had been forced in 1089 to help the failed Almoravid siege of Aledo.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line; the pages name towns (Jaén, Cabra, Aznalcázar, Écija, Málaga, Almería, Granada). The Granada core is Cliopatria's; the northern and eastern edges after 1073 are undocumented.

sources.title: Taifa of Granada
sources.note: Identity, rulers, Jaén c. 1028-1029, Seville 1036-1039, al-Funt 1038, Málaga 1056, Cabra 1079, the Almoravids September 1090.

sources.title: Zirid conquest of Málaga
sources.note: 1056, the Hammudid Yahya III al-Mahdi; says nothing about the districts annexed or about later Málaga.

sources.title: Taifa of Málaga
sources.note: Málaga to Granada 1057-1073, Tamim 1073-1090, Almoravids 1090; Écija 1039. Infobox gives no area.

sources.title: Taifa of Almería
sources.note: Almería's side of al-Funt and the Valencian occupation 1038-1042. Thin on Granada.

sources.title: Taifa of Seville
sources.note: Context only: Seville's 'greatest extent c. 1080'; it does not mention Ronda, Carmona or Morón and dates no conquest from Granada.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 1015-1065 draws Jaén's northern district from the start (the page has it taken c. 1028-1029) and omits Málaga until 1066 (the pages say 1056/57); the 1072 shape keeps Málaga after Tamim took it in 1073; 1085-1093 runs three years past the Almoravid conquest of September 1090. The infobox gives no area on any of the five pages, so no factor-of-two comparison was possible. Not settled (page silent): what land the Zirids 'took' from Almería in 1038 and 'to the west' in 1039; when and to whom Granada lost its northern and eastern edges by 1085 (Jaén, Baeza and Cabra are not dated); the parias paid to Alfonso VI in the 1080s (no years: the Castile dossier should carry the vassal_start with counterpart taifa-of-granada); the Siege of Granada (1018), Battle of Arjona (1041) and Battle of Cabra articles were not opened. Pages disagree on who governed Málaga after 1056 (son Buluggin or brother Tamim) and on 1056 versus 1057. Taifa of Málaga (1026-1090, Hammudid then Zirid then Tamim's) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier in this batch: it needs one (suggested slug taifa-of-malaga). Counterparts mirrored elsewhere: Seville (1036-1039 contest, Cabra 1079), Almería (vassal_start 1038), caliphate-of-cordoba (Jaén 1028), almoravid-dynasty (September 1090). Gazetteer names needed: Cabra, Écija, Aznalcázar (places, Córdoba and Seville provinces).
